Domestic institutions bought ₹8,930 crore — the largest single-day domestic purchase in the 39 sessions we hold. And UltraTech's entry into wires & cables repriced an entire industry.

The composite fell to 45.3 from 52.6, still inside the Neutral band.
The disagreement between its parts got wider, not narrower.
The spread between the strongest component (Volatility, 82.2) and the weakest (Breadth, 35.3) is now 46.9 points, up from 40.6 yesterday. Strip volatility out and the score is 41.3, not 45.3 — a four-point gap. Note what changed: yesterday the weakest link was Trend, a slow-moving structural measure. Today it is Breadth, which moves daily. The market is being held up by two things — how calm it is, and how hard domestic institutions are buying. Neither of those is the same as shares going up.

§3
What's Unusual Today
New India Assurance — 17.7% on 7.6x volume
The most unusual move in the market by a distance, scoring a perfect 100. NIACL rose 17.7% on 7.6x 3-month volume to a 52-week high of ₹229.30 (22.6% above 20SMA, RSI 78.7 overbought, ADX 39.6). Driven by market anticipation of the upcoming National Stock Exchange (NSE) IPO, where NIACL holds a 1.42% corporate equity stake.
Domestic buying at a 39-session record
5 of 39
Foreigners sold ₹3,112 Cr; domestic institutions bought ₹8,930 Cr —
the largest single day of all 39 sessions we hold
. DII absorption was 287%, completely insulating Indian equities from foreign exit ahead of US employment data.
HBL Engineering — 4.54% on 12.3x volume
The heaviest volume reading of the day at 12.3x normal volume for a modest 4.54% price move (RSI 51.1, 2.1% from 20SMA). Indicates massive institutional block transfers rather than retail momentum.
KEI Industries — down 8.95% on 5.5x volume (Tijori Industry Intel)
The day's worst faller on 5.5x volume (-12.8% below 20SMA, RSI 34). Triggered by UltraTech Cement's aggressive ₹1,800 Cr foray into cables ('Ultravolt' brand). Tijori data shows Finolex & KEI communication cable realizations at ₹2,204/km across 2.63M km annual sales; UltraTech's entrance threatens pricing power across incumbent cable makers.
Supreme Petrochem — 6.23% on 9.2x volume
Up 6.23% on 9.2x average volume (RSI 67, 8.3% above 20SMA). Low ADX of 14.3 indicates a fresh un-trended event driven by institutional positioning and polystyrene margin recovery expectations.
Tejas Networks — 8.23% on 6x volume (Tijori R&D Intel)
Up 8.23% on 6x volume (+15.4% above 20SMA, RSI 72.3). Powered by TCS's ₹1,537 Cr LOI for BSNL 4G/5G RAN equipment. Tijori operational metrics highlight Tejas maintaining R&D investments at 5.63% of total sales and 3.82x net sales per employee cost ratio.
Brigade Enterprises — 2.27% Giveback on Tijori Operational Strength
Realty standout Brigade announced 'Brigade Barcelona' in Hyderabad Neopolis corridor targeting ₹2,700 Cr GDV. Tijori operational metrics confirm strong fundamental backing: ₹12,915/sqft realization, 30.87M sqft area under construction, 76% hotel occupancy with ₹7,241 ADR (RevPAR ₹5,503), and low 7.61% borrowing cost.
Solar Industries — Tijori Order Book Intel (145.5% of Sales)
45 of 250
Maintained institutional focus amid South Africa acquisition clarifications. Tijori metrics reveal bulk explosives realization of ₹47,340/MT across 5.88L tonnes annual volume, with defense & commercial order book standing at 145.5% of annual revenue.
Oil & Gas breadth — 27-point swing in five sessions
1 of 24
The share of Nifty Oil and Gas constituents above their 20-day average rose 27 percentage points over five sessions, the largest move among all 24 indices, as Brent holds near $95 and refining margins firm.
Nifty 50 advance/decline at 0.88
116 of 246
0.88 shares rose for every one that fell — ranking 116th of 246 sessions. Demonstrates that market drama was concentrated in corporate catalysts rather than general market weakness.
Ranked by how unusual each reading is against its own history, not by which number is largest. Window lengths are in the pack; ranks shown as position out of window.

§4
Macro & Policy Dashboard
Forex reserves — an all-time high
$740.8bn
Released today · week ended 28 August · up $11.475bn
India's foreign exchange reserves rose $11.475 billion in a single week to a record
$740.803 billion
. This is the RBI's regular Friday release.
Foreign currency assets rose $9.337B to $600.67B; Gold holdings rose $2.191B to $116.409B.
Tijori banking data confirms the system has mobilised
$136.38 billion
via the RBI's special USD/INR swap facility, creating an impenetrable currency buffer.

(+8.2% YoY), confirming resilient domestic consumption.
Tijori auto dispatch feed shows strong festive channel stocking: Maruti Suzuki 1.76L units, TVS Motors 4.33L units, Hero MotoCorp 5.42L units.
The Rupee & Bond Yields
94.4310 / 6.94%
RBI Reference Rate & 10Y Benchmark
The rupee firmed to 94.43 per dollar, holding a two-month high despite $95 Brent crude.
India 10-year bond yield held near 6.94% as traders await August CPI data (Sept 12) following RBI's hawkish minutes.

Timing matters.
US markets close after India's. The Dow, Nasdaq and S&P figures above are 3 September closes — they were the cue for
today's
Indian open, and tonight's US session is the cue for Monday. They never explain the session being reported. Brent, gold, silver and the rupee trade through Indian hours and did move today.
The transmission chain, named.
Today reverses yesterday's chain almost exactly. Yesterday oil rose and fear rose with it; today one Federal Reserve official said inflation looked to be improving, US rate-hike odds fell, Wall Street had its best day in a month, and the effect travelled into India along three paths.
First
, into the open: the Sensex gapped up and snapped a four-day losing streak, and Nifty September futures moved from a short buildup to short covering.
Second
, into the currency: softer US rate expectations weakened the dollar, emerging-market currencies firmed, and the rupee held near a two-month high — which, combined with record reserves, is why India could absorb $95 oil without strain.
Third
, into safe havens, in reverse: gold fell 1.54% and silver 1.60% on MCX, unwinding yesterday's geopolitical bid. Where the chain did
not
reach is the domestic economy — 264 shares still fell, FMCG still has zero constituents above their 20-day average, and Auto breadth is down 46 points in five sessions. A friendlier global backdrop lifted the index; it did not fix what is wrong beneath it. And one purely domestic event, UltraTech's entry into wires and cables, overwhelmed all of it for an entire industry.

The board and the index disagreed again, but this time in the other direction. The Nifty 50 rose 0.10% and the Nifty 100 rose 0.04%, while the Nifty 500 was exactly flat, Midcap 100 fell 0.25% and Next 50 fell 0.23%. Only smallcaps joined the large caps, up 0.22%. That is a narrow advance: the gain lived in the biggest names. Over one week the picture is uniformly negative except smallcaps — the Nifty 50 down 1.15%, Next 50 down 1.72%, Midcap 100 down 1.55%, smallcaps up 0.08%. Over one month everything except smallcaps is still negative. The Nifty's own day was tight and unconvincing: it opened at 23,910.90, reached 24,005.75, and closed at 23,897.70 — below its open, in the lower third of a 109.9-point range that was the narrowest in weeks. An index that gaps up on a strong global cue and then spends the day drifting back has not been bought; it has been carried.

A/D D-1
is the advance/decline for yesterday.
%>20D D-1
is the percentage of stocks in that index trading above their 20-day SMA, yesterday.
A/D Today
tells you how the index performed today — what the advance-to-decline ratio was.
%>20D SMA
tells you what percentage of stocks in that universe is trading above its 20-day simple moving average. Watch how the A/D ratio moved from last week to today, and how %>20D SMA moved over the same stretch — those two shaded pairs are the comparison this table exists for.
A rising index with
increasing advances and more stocks above the 20D SMA
means broader participation in the rally. A rising index on
very narrow participation
can instead mean index management, indecision, or only a few sectors doing the work while the rest of the market goes nowhere.
Eight sectors moved enough in breadth to flag. They split into a banking-and-energy group that is quietly strengthening and a manufacturing-and-defensive group that is deteriorating fast.
NIFTY IT
— the worst breadth for a second consecutive day: 0.25, meaning four constituents fell for every one that rose, and the share above the 20-day average has now dropped 40 points in three sessions to 30%. The sector index fell 0.47% and is down 1.88% over the week. This is the same structural story — Nifty IT is down roughly 29% in 2026 on fears that AI tooling erodes the traditional services model — and the bounce we flagged yesterday has now been fully surrendered.
NIFTY HEALTHCARE
— breadth of 0.18, worse than IT: roughly five constituents fell for every one that rose. The share above the 20-day average is 25% after a 20-point drop in three sessions, and the sector index fell 0.87%, the worst of any sector today. Over one week it is down 2.32%. Pharma fell 0.68% alongside it and has lost 15 points of breadth. Two sectors that were 7th and 4th ranked a month ago are now unwinding together, with no news attached — the signature of a crowded position being exited.
NIFTY PSU BANK
— the share above the 20-day average rose 25 points in three sessions to 50%, one of the largest improvements on the board. But note the tension: today's advance/decline was only 0.83, and the index fell 0.44%. Breadth improving over three sessions while price falls today is a normal, healthy pause, not a reversal.
NIFTY CAPITAL GOODS
— the day's most dramatic reversal. Yesterday 3.17 constituents rose for every one that fell; today 0.61. It still supplied 9 of the 40 scanner names from a 50-stock index, 2.25 times its fair share — but where yesterday 8 of 10 were gainers, today 6 of 9 are losers: KEI, Polycab, Finolex Cables, Kirloskar Oil Engines, Thermax and Jyoti CNC, against gains in Carborundum Universal, HBL Engineering and APL Apollo. Finolex Cables and Jyoti CNC were
gainers
in this same table yesterday. The UltraTech announcement is doing most of this work.
NIFTY REALTY
— a sharp giveback. Yesterday's best sector, up 2.58%, fell 0.90% today with an advance/decline of 0.25 — four constituents down for every one up. Brigade, yesterday's 11.3% star, dropped 2.27% on above-average volume. The five-day breadth trend is still positive at +10 points and the sector remains 2nd over one month and up 18.74% over three, so this reads as profit-taking after a vertical day rather than a change of direction.
NIFTY AUTO
— the most damaged sector in the market. An advance/decline of 0.15 means roughly seven constituents fell for every one that rose. Just
7% are above their 20-day average
— one stock in fifteen. Breadth is down 46 points over five sessions, by far the worst on the board, and the index has fallen 3.95% in a week and 4.58% in a month. This is now deterioration on every measure at once.
NIFTY METAL
— the one clear bright spot. 2.75 constituents rose for every one that fell, the index gained 1.07% — the best sector of the day — and 53% now sit above their 20-day average. This resolves the contradiction we flagged yesterday, when every MCX metal rose but metal shares lost 27 points of breadth. Today the shares followed, even though the metals themselves fell. APL Apollo was the sector's scanner name.
NIFTY FMCG
—
a second consecutive day with zero of fifteen constituents above their 20-day average.
The advance/decline was 0.36 and the index fell 0.14%, and it remains the worst sector over one month at −7.34% and over three months at −4.82%. Two days at absolute zero breadth is no longer a single bad session; it is a sector where not one constituent can hold a short-term average.

§14
Tomorrow's Action Plan
23,900 on the option chain
Confirms if: Holding it keeps 12.63 million put contracts in profit and the market pinned in its 100-point box into Tuesday. Put writers moved their floor up 300 points to get here — they will defend it.
Denies it if: Losing it turns the largest put position in the chain into a forced unwind, with nothing priced for the move. This is now the single most important level on the page.
Whether breadth can hold above 1.0 for two consecutive days
Confirms if: It has not managed this all week — 0.49, then 1.51, then 0.88. Two good days in a row would be the first evidence the broad market is participating rather than oscillating.
Denies it if: Another sub-1.0 reading on Monday, with the index up, means the advance keeps narrowing into fewer and larger names. That is how tops are built.
Auto breadth off 7%
Confirms if: One stock in fifteen above its 20-day average is close to the floor. Any recovery here would relieve the worst-damaged sector on the board.
Denies it if: Auto has now lost 46 points of breadth in five sessions and 4.58% in a month. If this keeps falling it stops being a sector problem and becomes a consumption problem, alongside FMCG at zero.
Whether the cables de-rating spreads
Confirms if: If KEI, Polycab and RR Kabel stabilise on Monday, today was a one-day repricing of a competitive threat and the market has taken its medicine.
Denies it if: Further falls would say investors are re-examining every business where the Aditya Birla Group could plausibly arrive next. Note this is its fourth new business in three years — the pattern is the risk, not this one entry.
The rupee's distance from 95.00
Confirms if: Two days of strength on record $740.8bn reserves is a genuine buffer. While this holds, India can absorb $95 oil without the usual damage.
Denies it if: A drift back toward 95.00 would mean the swap-facility inflows have run their course, and the oil bill starts to bite again.
India VIX at 10.62
Confirms if: Cheap protection. If you want downside insurance, it has rarely cost less — only 45 of the last 250 sessions were calmer.
Denies it if: A market this quiet with Hormuz traffic at six vessels a day against a norm of thirteen is not pricing its own risk. Complacency is not the same as safety.

Bull triggers
Domestic institutions bought ₹8,930 crore, the largest single day in our 39-session record, and ₹23,156 crore across this week alone.
The Sensex snapped a four-day losing streak, and Wall Street had its best day in a month as US rate-hike fears eased.
Forex reserves hit an all-time high of $740.803bn, up $11.475bn in one week — a real buffer against $95 oil.
The rupee held near a two-month high for a second session, with the RBI's swap facility having mobilised $136.38bn.
September futures moved from short buildup to short covering, and the put floor jumped 300 points to sit right at the money.
All three banking indices and oil and gas are in the top five for five-day breadth gains — the rotation has a coherent destination.
Nifty Metal rose 1.07%, finally resolving the disconnect where metal shares were falling while metal prices rose.
Bear triggers
264 shares fell against 233 that rose. A record domestic purchase bought the Nifty just 24 points.
The Nifty closed below its open and in the lower third of its range, on the narrowest day in weeks.
The index remains 2.9% below its 200-day average, and Breadth has replaced Trend as the weakest regime component.
FMCG has zero of fifteen constituents above their 20-day average for a second consecutive day.
Auto has 7% above their 20-day average and has lost 46 points of breadth in five sessions — the worst on the board.
IT and healthcare are unwinding together with no news attached, both down 20 to 25 points of breadth.
One corporate announcement erased up to 9% from an entire industry in a session, which says valuations were carrying no margin for competitive surprise.
India VIX at 10.62 is a six-week low while Hormuz traffic runs at half its normal rate. The market is not pricing the risk it is carrying.
Two facts sit awkwardly together today. Domestic institutions made their largest single-day purchase in our entire record — ₹8,930 crore — and the Nifty went up 24 points while 264 shares fell. Money that size normally moves an index further than that. When it does not, it is because someone is selling into it, and the foreign sale of ₹3,112 crore only accounts for part of the other side. The global backdrop genuinely improved: rate-hike fears eased, Wall Street had its best day in a month, the rupee held near a two-month high on record reserves, and gold and silver gave back their fear premium. That is what lifted the index. What it did not lift is the domestic economy's own sectors — auto at 7% breadth, FMCG at zero for a second day, healthcare and IT unwinding in tandem. And the day's loudest event was neither global nor macro: one cement company announced it was entering the wires business, and an entire industry lost up to 9%. That is what a market with no margin for surprise looks like. The option chain has narrowed to a 100-point box between 23,900 and 24,000, and India VIX has fallen to 10.62. Watch 23,900 — the put writers moved their floor 300 points to defend it, and almost nothing is priced for them being wrong.

GUIDE & METHODOLOGY
How to Read This Report
The order matters more than the sections. Most readers open at the index level and stop there — which is the habit that makes a narrow market look healthy.
Step 1
Start with participation, not the index
Open §7. Which direction is the number of stocks above their 20-day average moving? That is the market’s direction of travel, not the index close.
Step 2
Then check the index against it
If the Nifty rose but fewer stocks are above their 20-day average than yesterday, participation is falling inside a rising index. That divergence is the most important thing on the page.
Step 3
Read sector leadership across timeframes
In §6b, compare each sector’s 1-day move against its 1-week and 1-month bars. A sector strong on the day but weak on the month is a bounce. A sector strong on all three is a trend.
Step 4
Cross-check each sector’s move against its own breadth
A sector that rose today but whose participation column is falling has a narrow move — a few stocks doing the work. §6b row next to §7 row is the comparison.
Step 5
Go straight to the flagged sectors
The pack has already joined breadth to the scanners for you. Read §7’s notable flags and §9’s scanner names together — that join is already done.
Step 6
Ask whether the money agrees with the positioning
Compare §11 (what institutions bought and sold) with §13 (where the derivatives positioning sits). Conviction shows when both point the same way.
